label: MODELED / ANALYTIC ASSESSMENT

inputs.nbga: USGS Geochemical Database for the Brackish Groundwater Assessment of the United States, Dissolved-Solids Dataset
inputs.swd: Railroad Commission of Texas, layers 4 Injection/Disposal and 3 Commercial Disposal
inputs.pwdb: USGS National Produced Waters Geochemical Database v3.0 (Blondes et al.; Scanlon et al. compilation)
inputs.datacenters: FracTracker Alliance U.S. Data Centers Tracker (via University of Oregon ArcGIS feature layer)
inputs.usgs_quakes: USGS Earthquake Catalog (ComCat) FDSN event service
inputs.usdm: US Drought Monitor (NDMC, USDA, NOAA), current weekly map
inputs.aqueduct: Kuzma, S., Bierkens, M.F.P., Lakshman, S., Luo, T., Saccoccia, L., Sutanudjaja, E.H., Van Beek, R. 2023. Aqueduct 4.0: Updated decision-relevant global water risk indicators. Technical Note. Washington, DC: World Resources Institute.

formula: s_brackish = (share of NBGA samples within 0.5 degrees with 1,000-10,000 mg/L TDS) x min(1, samples/20)
s_produced = log10(1 + injection/disposal wells within 50 km) / log10(1 + 95th-percentile cell value)
s_stress = 0.5 x (Aqueduct 4.0 Texas baseline water stress / 5) + 0.5 x (US Drought Monitor class at cell centre, D0=1 ... D4=5, / 5; 0 if none)
s_demand = log10(1 + tracked data centers within 50 km, excluding cancelled) / log10(1 + 95th-percentile cell value)
score = 100 x (0.30 s_brackish + 0.30 s_produced + 0.25 s_stress + 0.15 s_demand)
caveats: Injection/disposal well counts are a proxy for produced-water presence; RRC does not publish per-well volumes in the layer used.
Aqueduct stress is one value for all of Texas, so spatial variation in s_stress comes only from drought class.
Not a permitting, engineering or cost assessment. Treatment feasibility depends on salinity, brine management and energy (see the published paper).
